findings.problem: Status is stored as a raw String, allowing any arbitrary value. No type-level enforcement of valid states or transitions.
findings.failure_mode: PacketWorkflow can hold status values like "cancelled", "", "DELETED", or any future typo, making invalid state representable at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace with `pub status: PacketStatus` enum where `PacketStatus` variants are `New`, `Validated`, `Sent`. The mark_sent function should construct the Sent variant directly.

findings.problem: Lifecycle state is encoded as a standalone bool. This is not a typestate machine — no transitions are enforced and no ordering is encoded.
findings.failure_mode: PacketWorkflow can be marked is_validated=false while status="sent", or is_validated=true with status="", representing impossible/inconsistent workflow states.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single typestate enum that encodes the full lifecycle: `enum PacketStatus { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`.

findings.problem: The struct has no typestate transitions. Any caller can set any field to any value. There is no smart constructor, no transition function, and no invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create PacketWorkflow with status="sent", is_sent=false, is_validated=true simultaneously — an internally inconsistent state that no domain logic would ever produce.
findings.fix: Replace struct fields with a status enum carrying lifecycle data. Provide a `PacketWorkflow::new(id)` constructor. Provide `fn validated(self) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, Error>` and `fn sent(self, epoch_ms: u64) -> PacketWorkflow` as the only transitions.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an independent Option separate from the boolean is_sent flag. When is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms=None, the packet claims to be sent with no timestamp. When is_sent=false but sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(...), the packet has a sent timestamp but claims not sent.
findings.failure_mode: Querying sent packets with None timestamps returns incorrect data; reverse inconsistency (timestamp set but not sent) leaks internal timing data.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the status enum: `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`. The timestamp is then required when and only when the packet is in the Sent state.

findings.construct: pub struct PacketWorkflow { pub id: String, ... }
findings.problem: No smart constructor exists. Any caller can instantiate PacketWorkflow with empty id, invalid status strings, and inconsistent flag combinations.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code receives PacketWorkflow with id="" or inconsistent state, causing silent misbehavior or incorrect queries.
findings.fix: Provide `fn new(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketError::EmptyId>` as the sole constructor. Use a `PacketId` newtype with validation instead of raw String.

findings.problem: Packet ID is a raw String with no domain semantics encoded. Empty strings, duplicate IDs, or non-ASCII identifiers are all representable.
findings.failure_mode: Collision or ambiguity when IDs lack unique/parse guarantees; no domain-level enforcement of ID format or uniqueness.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct PacketId(String)` with a smart constructor that validates the ID format (non-empty, length cap). Use `pub id: PacketId` in the struct.

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally allocates a new String for the status field, even when status is already "sent". No fallible reserve, no capacity check, and no early return if status is already set.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation on every mark_sent call; repeated calls to mark_sent are no-ops but keep allocating.
findings.fix: With an enum typestate, mark_sent becomes `fn mark_sent(self, epoch_ms: u64) -> PacketWorkflow { Self { status: PacketStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: epoch_ms }, .. } }` — no heap allocation, no String::to_string.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs heap allocation to convert a string literal into an owned String. This is an imperative side effect in what should be a pure state transition function.
findings.failure_mode: Hidden allocation makes the function's cost unpredictable and non-deterministic under memory pressure.
findings.fix: Use an enum typestate where the Sent variant carries only the u64 timestamp. No allocation needed for the status tag.

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: PacketWorkflow) -> PacketWorkflow
findings.problem: No Error enum exists for this module. Invalid state transitions (e.g., marking sent when already sent, or sending without prior validation) have no typed failure path.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot distinguish between successful transition, already-sent state, or pre-condition failure. Silent no-ops replace explicit errors.
findings.fix: Define `enum PacketError { AlreadySent, NotValidated }`. Change signature to `fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketError>`.

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: PacketWorkflow) -> PacketWorkflow
findings.problem: Function takes and returns PacketWorkflow by value, forcing full struct move on every transition instead of accepting a reference and returning a new or modified instance.
findings.failure_mode: Caller loses their original PacketWorkflow; no ability to perform dry-run or conditional transitions.
findings.fix: Use `fn mark_sent(packet: PacketWorkflow, epoch_ms: u64) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketError>` with ownership transfer only on success.
